title: Regional traffic sentinel and automated rollout safeguards for Hosted API
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Harden the Hosted API deployment pipeline with an automated ‘traffic sentinel’ layer that enforces SLO-aware rollout gates across blue/green and regional traffic shifts. This ticket implements control-plane checks, automatic rollback triggers, and a human-in-the-loop escalation path for cross-region releases.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: staged traffic ramps (regional + zone-level), sentinel heuristics (latency/error/queue), centralized audit events for every traffic shift, operator override API, and integration with Console dashboards and incident runbooks.
- Out of scope: on-prem deployment automation and Dedicated capacity autoscaler tuning (tracked separately).

Acceptance criteria:
- New sentinel service can block or pause a rollout when configured SLOs degrade beyond thresholds (p95 latency increase >25% AND error rate increase >0.5pp sustained for 2m).
- Rollouts can be started with a declarative policy (initial weight, ramp profile, holdpoints) and either complete automatically or escalate to paging.
- All traffic shift decisions produce immutable audit events (who/what/why) visible in Console and persisted to the event store.
- Manual override endpoints exist for engineering and SRE roles with RBAC and MFA guardrails.

Design decisions and rationale:
- Sentinel lives in the control plane (not data plane) to avoid adding token-level latency to RPC paths. This allows fast gating decisions based on aggregated metrics while keeping per-request paths unchanged.
- Use SLO-composite checks (latency + error + queue depth) rather than single-metric thresholds to reduce noisy aborts during transient spikes.
- Favor deterministic, small-step ramps (e.g., 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%) with configurable dwell times. We will default to conservative ramps for cross-region cutovers.
- Implement a short-circuit rollback path when certain catastrophic conditions occur (node OOMs, 5xx spike >3pp, or global request queue >90th percentile threshold) so customers experience minimal degradation.

Operational hooks and metrics to emit:
- rollout.started, rollout.step.completed, rollout.paused, rollout.rolled_back, rollout.finalized (with tags: region, model_version, operator).
- sentinel.decision.reason (string tag), sentinel.slo_scores (numeric), and sentinel.latency_delta_p95.
- dashboards: per-rollout timeline, heatmap of regional p95 deltas, and a single-pane-of-glass for active rollouts.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Automation vs human control: aggressive automation lowers MTTR but increases risk of incorrect rollbacks for benign regressions. Current approach: conservative default automation + opt-in aggressive policies for vetted partners.
- Storage of audit events: we will write to the existing event-store for retention and to Dynamo for quick lookup (cost vs query-latency trade-off).
- Canary size heuristics for low-traffic regions: when a region has low absolute qps, relative error spikes are noisy. We will add absolute minimum query thresholds before triggering gates.

Integration points (PRs & docs):
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/2026-Regional+Traffic+Sentinel+Design
- PoC service PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sentinel/pull/186
- Console dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood-infra.com/d/rollouts/hosted-api-rollout-timeline?orgId=1
- Runbook stub: https://docs.redwood-infra.com/runbooks/rollout-sentinel-escalation

Risks and mitigation:
- False positives during region-level noisy neighbors: mitigate with composite SLOs and minimum sample sizes.
- RBAC/override abuse: require two-person approval for destructive rollbacks in production.
- Increased control-plane load during large-scale coordinated cutovers: add rate limiting and backpressure on the sentinel ingestion pipeline and test with synthetic load.

Next steps:
1) Complete the sentinel PoC PR and add e2e test that simulates a p95 regression.
2) Wire-up Console events and implement an immutable audit stream.
3) Run staged chaos tests on staging (cross-region latency injection) and validate rollback semantics.
4) Security review for manual override endpoints.

Owners: Marcus Patel (engineering lead), SRE: Priya Kumar, PM: Liam O'Connor
updates: 2026-02-16 - Kickoff: scoped work with SRE and Console teams; agreed on composite SLO approach. Action: Marcus to deliver PoC by end of week.
2026-02-22 - PoC PR opened (link in attachments). Basic decision engine implemented; currently uses p95 and 5xx rate. Feedback from SRE: add queue-depth signal and minimum-sample gating.
2026-02-27 - Design review with PM and Console. Console will expose ‘pause’ button wired to sentinel API; audit schema agreed. PM requested clearer UX for escalation — added to next iteration.
2026-03-05 - Added deterministic ramp profiles and holdpoint configuration. QA: need an automated test harness to simulate regional traffic patterns before ship.
2026-03-10 - Security review kickoff: initial concerns about single-actor rollback; plan to require two approvals for production rollbacks. Security team assigned follow-up tasks.

2026-03-12 - Integration test run in staging: simulated p95 spike triggered pause correctly; rollback path exercised and audit event recorded. Minor bug: console timeline lagged by 15s, raised ENG-66422 to address the event fan-out pipeline.
